answer.rationale: Two hypotheses compete: (a) the release 2 hours ago introduced a write-path regression — supported by latency starting to climb ~30 min after deploy, consistent with a gradual resource/leak pattern; (b) a primary-region infrastructure issue — supported by the degradation being region-confined and traffic being at daily settlement peak. The temporal coupling to the release is the stronger signal, and memory_b1 documents that rolling back to the prior stable build cleared a similar spike quickly and without customer impact; I am verifying that record before committing since it grounds the highest-stakes claim. Rollback is preferred over failover (memory_b2) because failing over during peak settlement write load risks in-flight write loss and would not fix a code regression that would follow traffic to the new region. Add-capacity (memory_b3 pattern) treats symptoms, not a suspected regression, and is slow. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing target dependency/read load, but the degradation is on the write path. Rollback is reversible and preserves writes on the known-stable prior build; if latency does not recover post-rollback, regional failover becomes the next-window action.
